title: Pulmonary fibrosis, scleroderma lung, tracheostomy and ventilator
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's lung fibrosis or airway status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Shortness of breath.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old woman presenting for a follow-up regarding persistent shortness of breath and a dry cough. She reports that the symptoms have gradually worsened over the past several months, particularly during physical exertion. She denies any recent fevers, chills, or productive cough. A recent chest CT scan was performed, which revealed evidence of pulmonary fibrosis. The underlying cause of the pulmonary fibrosis is currently not determined.

Medication List
Multivitamin, Lisinopril 10mg daily.

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. Breath sounds are diminished in the lower lobes with some crackles noted. Oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. No cyanosis or peripheral edema noted.

Assessment
The patient has pulmonary fibrosis. The etiology of the pulmonary fibrosis remains unknown at this time.

Plan
A referral to pulmonology was placed today to further evaluate the extent of the pulmonary fibrosis and to discuss management options. The patient will be instructed to monitor her symptoms and follow up with the specialist.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pulmonary fibrosis without a documented cause: J84.10 (HCC 280).
